pages.title: Overview
pages.description: The layers of chan, from a terminal to devservers and gateways, and where each is taught.

pages.title: Install and first run
pages.description: Install Chan Desktop, open the Computers screen, and make a first terminal and workspace.
pages.head: launcher-demo

pages.title: Concepts
pages.description: Workspaces, libraries, windows, the Computers screen, devservers and gateways, and how each layer builds on the one before.

pages.title: Terminal basics
pages.description: Terminal tabs and names, find in scrollback, copy and paste, group broadcast, and what each terminal runs.

pages.title: Windows, panes and tabs
pages.description: Split a window into panes, keep two sides of tabs in each, drag tabs, and rearrange the layout with Hybrid Nav.

pages.title: Command launcher
pages.description: Run any command, change a setting, or reach any window from one searchable list.

pages.title: Rich Prompt and drafts
pages.description: Write long Markdown prompts with images for the agent in a terminal, and keep notes as drafts outside your project.

pages.title: Script it with cs
pages.description: Drive the window and its terminals from a shell: open files, write to and read terminals, report status, and arrange panes.

pages.title: tmux control mode
pages.description: Run tmux -CC in a chan terminal, locally or over ssh, and work with its windows and panes as Chan windows and panes.

pages.title: Agent teams
pages.description: Start a lead and worker agents in named terminals from a dialog or cs, and give agents the workspace over MCP.

pages.title: Workspaces and chan serve
pages.description: Register a directory as a workspace, choose where chan serve runs it, turn it on or off, and list, close, or forget it.

pages.title: Editor
pages.description: Open and edit files, write Markdown with links, mentions, tags and dates, and handle saves that conflict with other programs.

pages.title: Previews, slides and export
pages.description: Preview and present slide decks, draw Mermaid and Excalidraw diagrams, view JSON and CSV, and export to PDF.

pages.title: File browser
pages.description: Browse and manage files from the keyboard, upload and download them, and read code reports with COCOMO estimates.

pages.title: Search
pages.description: Find content, files, tags and contacts in a workspace, and query or walk its graph from a terminal with cs search.

pages.title: Graph
pages.description: Explore a workspace's tree with its links, tags and mentions, open directories in place, and use depth to see more.

pages.title: Dashboard and index
pages.description: Watch the serving process's metrics, read workspace facts, follow indexing, and turn on semantic search.

pages.title: Extensions
pages.description: Add your own web apps as tabs, configure their declarations, and build one that drives chan through cs.

pages.title: Computers screen
pages.description: See every machine and window in one place, open terminals and workspaces, and show or hide windows from the keyboard.

pages.title: Standalone terminal, files and editor
pages.description: A window with no workspace, the chan-term, chan-files and chan-edit commands, and Chan Desktop as a default app.

pages.title: Settings
pages.description: Every Settings section, the defaults worth knowing, chan config from a shell, and what privacy mode hides.

pages.title: Screen lock and animations
pages.description: Lock a workspace window after idle time or at once, with an optional PIN, and play animations in an empty pane.

pages.title: Remote overview
pages.description: Compare the routes to a devserver: a browser, a direct address, ssh, Eternal Terminal, Lima or WSL, and a gateway.

pages.title: Run a devserver
pages.description: Install chan on another machine, run its devserver as a service, and manage its token and metrics.

pages.title: systemd integration
pages.description: Run the devserver as a systemd user service, restart and upgrade it without losing terminals, and report its metrics to systemd-report.

pages.title: Connect from Chan Desktop
pages.description: Add a devserver with its connect script, use the control terminal, recover from dropped connections, and open remote windows.

pages.title: Chan in a browser
pages.description: Serve a workspace or a devserver to any browser with the chan binary alone, and keep windows running behind closed tabs.

pages.title: Tunnels, transfers and clipboard
pages.description: Forward ports from a devserver, upload and download files, and copy and paste across machines with cs.

pages.title: Collaboration
pages.description: Share a workspace between windows and people, manage connected clients with cs session, and hand over session leadership.

pages.title: Connect to a gateway
pages.description: Add a self-hosted gateway to Chan Desktop, sign in, open and share devservers, and reach it through WireGuard.

pages.title: Keyboard shortcuts
pages.description: Every default key on macOS, Windows, Linux and in a browser, and how to change one.

pages.title: Commands
pages.description: Every chan command and subcommand, the chan serve flags no other page covers, and the other names of the chan binary.

pages.title: Troubleshooting
pages.description: What a message or a stuck window means, its likely cause and its fix: Chan Desktop, devservers, cs, chan serve, tmux and Linux defaults.

pages.title: Plan and prerequisites
pages.description: What a gateway runs, and the server, DNS records, certificate and OAuth app it needs before you install.

pages.title: Install
pages.description: Create the gateway's Postgres database and install the service packages on an Ubuntu server.

pages.title: Configure
pages.description: Run the setup script, apply the database schema, and start the gateway services.

pages.title: The edge proxy
pages.description: Put nginx in front of the gateway to terminate TLS and route sign-in, tunnels and devserver pages.

pages.title: Accounts and sign-in
pages.description: Let yourself in, set your username, and choose who else may sign in to the gateway.

pages.title: Publish a devserver
pages.description: Dial a devserver in with an access token, open it in a browser or Chan Desktop, and share it.

pages.title: WireGuard
pages.description: Let Chan Desktop reach the proxy nodes through WireGuard, with keys the gateway enrolls at sign-in.

pages.title: Operate
pages.description: Run the gateway day to day: the admin CLI, more proxy nodes, upgrades, health checks and logs.
